title: Java Programming - MSBTE 314317 (K Scheme) - 4th Semester - Question Bank (150 Qs)

units.unit: Unit I - Basic Syntactical Constructs in Java

questions.question: Which of the following is not a Java keyword?
questions.answer: Boolean
questions.explanation: 'Boolean' is a wrapper class; Java keyword for primitive type is 'boolean' (lowercase).

questions.question: What is the default value of an instance variable of type int in Java?
questions.explanation: Instance numeric types default to 0; object references default to null.

questions.question: Define a constructor in Java.
questions.answer: A constructor is a special method that initializes a newly created object and has the same name as the class with no return type.
questions.explanation: Constructors set initial state and may be overloaded; they do not have a return type.

questions.question: Which operator is used for reference comparison in Java?
questions.explanation: The '==' operator compares object references (addresses); equals() compares logical equality if overridden.

questions.question: What is autoboxing in Java?
questions.answer: Autoboxing is automatic conversion between primitive types (like int) and their wrapper classes (like Integer).
questions.explanation: Introduced in Java 5 to ease conversion between primitives and wrapper objects.

questions.question: Which class is mutable among the following?
questions.answer: Both B and C
questions.explanation: StringBuffer and StringBuilder are mutable; String is immutable.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the main method signature to start a Java program?
questions.answer: public static void main(String args[])
questions.explanation: Standard entry point requires public static void with a String array parameter.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'final' keyword when applied to a variable?
questions.answer: final makes a variable a constant so its value cannot be changed after initialization.
questions.explanation: Final variables must be initialized once; for objects, the reference can't change (object can mutate).

questions.question: Which conversion is NOT allowed implicitly in Java?
questions.answer: double to float
questions.explanation: double to float is narrowing and requires explicit cast; others are widening conversions.

questions.question: Explain what the 'scope' of a variable means.
questions.answer: Scope defines the region of code where a variable is accessible (local, instance, class/static scope).
questions.explanation: Local variables visible within block/method; instance variables accessible within object methods; static variables via class.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct way to declare an array of integers in Java?
questions.answer: Both A and B
questions.explanation: Both syntaxes are valid for declaring arrays in Java.

questions.question: What is the difference between String and StringBuffer?
questions.answer: String is immutable; StringBuffer is mutable and synchronized (thread-safe).
questions.explanation: Modifying a String creates new objects; StringBuffer allows in-place modifications and is synchronized.

questions.question: What will be the output of: System.out.println(10 + 20 + "30" + 40); ?
questions.explanation: 10+20 evaluated first =30, then "30" makes subsequent concatenations produce "3030" + 40 = "303040".

questions.question: What are wrapper classes in Java? Give two examples.
questions.answer: Wrapper classes are object representations of primitive types, e.g., Integer for int, Double for double.
questions.explanation: They allow primitives to be treated as objects and used in collections and generics.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to inherit a class in Java?
questions.answer: extends
questions.explanation: extends is used for class-to-class inheritance; implements is for interfaces.

questions.question: What is method overloading?
questions.answer: Method overloading is defining multiple methods in the same class with the same name but different parameter lists.
questions.explanation: Return type can differ but signature must vary by parameter types/count/order.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about 'static' is TRUE?
options: Static methods can access instance variables directly
Static variables belong to the class
Static cannot be used with methods
questions.answer: Static variables belong to the class
questions.explanation: Static members are class-level and shared across all instances.

questions.question: What is garbage collection in Java?
questions.answer: Garbage collection is automatic memory management that reclaims memory of objects no longer reachable.
questions.explanation: JVM's GC runs to free unused heap objects to avoid memory leaks.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid main method parameter declaration?
questions.answer: All of the above
questions.explanation: All shown parameter declarations are valid ways to accept command-line arguments.

questions.question: Explain the difference between == and equals() when comparing Strings.
questions.answer: == compares reference identity, equals() compares String contents (characters) when overridden.
questions.explanation: Use equals() to check two strings for same sequence of characters, not ==.

questions.question: Which collection class preserves insertion order and allows null elements?
questions.answer: ArrayList
questions.explanation: ArrayList preserves insertion order and allows nulls; HashSet doesn't guarantee order.

questions.question: What is a symbolic constant in Java and how is it declared?
questions.answer: A symbolic constant is a final variable declared using 'final' and usually 'static' (e.g., public static final int MAX=100;).
questions.explanation: final prevents reassignment; static final is common for constants accessible at class level.

questions.question: Which of these access specifiers allows access from same package only?
questions.answer: default (no modifier)
questions.explanation: Default (package-private) access restricts visibility to classes within same package.

questions.question: What does 'command line arguments' refer to in Java?
questions.answer: Command line arguments are tokens passed to the program on startup accessible through the main method's String[] args parameter.
questions.explanation: They allow users to pass input values when launching the Java program from a shell.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about local variables in Java?
options: They must be initialized before use
questions.answer: They must be initialized before use
questions.explanation: Local variables are not initialized by default and must be explicitly assigned before use.

units.unit: Unit II - Inheritance, Interface and Packages

questions.question: Which type of inheritance is not supported directly by Java for classes?
questions.answer: Multiple inheritance (class-class)
questions.explanation: Java does not allow multiple inheritance with classes to avoid ambiguity; interfaces can be multiply implemented.

questions.question: What is method overriding?
questions.answer: Method overriding is redefining a superclass method in a subclass with the same signature to provide specific implementation.
questions.explanation: Overriding enables runtime polymorphism when methods are invoked on subclass instances via superclass references.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to refer to the immediate parent class constructor or members?
questions.answer: super
questions.explanation: 'super' accesses parent class members and constructors from a subclass.

questions.question: Give two differences between abstract class and interface (pre-Java 8).
questions.answer: Abstract classes can have constructors and instance fields; interfaces (pre-Java 8) can only have abstract methods and constants.
questions.explanation: Abstract classes can store state; interfaces before Java 8 were purely abstract method contracts.

questions.question: Which statement about interfaces in Java is TRUE (Java 7/8 basic concept)?
options: Interfaces can have private instance fields
Interfaces can contain method implementations only since Java 1.0
A class can implement multiple interfaces
questions.answer: A class can implement multiple interfaces
questions.explanation: Classes may implement many interfaces enabling multiple inheritance of type.

questions.question: What is the purpose of packages in Java?
questions.answer: Packages organize related classes/interfaces, provide namespace management, and control access protection across modules.
questions.explanation: They help avoid naming conflicts and group logically related code.

questions.question: Which of following is correct about 'final' when applied to a class?
options: It prevents class from being instantiated
It prevents class from being subclassed
questions.answer: It prevents class from being subclassed
questions.explanation: A final class cannot be extended; its methods can still be invoked and objects instantiated.

questions.question: Explain the use of 'package' and 'import' keywords with an example.
questions.answer: package declares the class's package (e.g., package com.college;), import brings other packages' classes into scope (e.g., import java.util.List;).
questions.explanation: package groups classes; import avoids fully-qualified names in code.

questions.question: Which access modifier allows a subclass in a different package to access a member?
questions.answer: protected
questions.explanation: protected permits access by subclasses and classes in the same package.

questions.question: What is multiple inheritance of type in Java?
questions.answer: Multiple inheritance of type allows a class to implement multiple interfaces, thus inheriting multiple type contracts.
questions.explanation: Java supports multiple interface implementation to achieve multiple type inheritance safely.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'super()' when used in subclass constructor?
options: Creates a new object of superclass type
questions.answer: Calls parent class's no-arg constructor
questions.explanation: super() invokes the superclass constructor; must be first statement in subclass constructor.

questions.question: How do you create a user-defined package and use it in another class?
questions.answer: Place classes in a folder structure matching package name, declare 'package packname;' at top, compile and import using 'import packname.ClassName;'.
questions.explanation: Use correct package declaration and classpath to access user-defined package classes.

questions.question: If class A extends B and B extends C, what type of inheritance is this?
questions.answer: Multilevel inheritance
questions.explanation: Inheritance chain through multiple levels (C -> B -> A) is multilevel.

questions.question: What is 'interface' default method (brief)?
questions.answer: A default method in interface (Java 8+) provides a default implementation allowing interfaces to evolve without breaking implementations.
questions.explanation: Declared with 'default' keyword; implementing classes may override it.

questions.question: Which is the correct statement to import all classes of package java.util?
questions.answer: import java.util.*;
questions.explanation: import with wildcard brings all public classes/interfaces of package into scope.

questions.question: Why might you declare a class abstract?
questions.answer: Declare class abstract if it contains abstract methods (no implementation) or should not be instantiated directly while providing shared code for subclasses.
questions.explanation: Abstract classes define common behavior and allow subclasses to implement specifics.

questions.question: Which of these members are inherited by subclass?
questions.answer: protected methods
questions.explanation: Protected and public members are inherited; private members are not directly accessible in subclass.

questions.question: Explain 'static import' and give a use-case.
questions.answer: Static import allows direct access to static members without class qualifier, e.g., 'import static java.lang.Math.*;' to use sqrt() directly.
questions.explanation: It improves readability when many static members are used frequently.

questions.question: What does 'implements' keyword do in a class declaration?
options: Indicates class provides implementations for interface methods
questions.answer: Indicates class provides implementations for interface methods
questions.explanation: implements binds a class to contract specified by interface(s) and requires method implementations.

questions.question: What happens if a class implements an interface but does not implement all methods?
questions.answer: The class must be declared abstract or else compilation error occurs until all interface methods are implemented.
questions.explanation: Unimplemented interface methods force the class to be abstract.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a feature of packages?
questions.answer: Automatic memory management
questions.explanation: Packages organize code and provide access controls; memory management is JVM responsibility.

questions.question: What is 'naming convention' for packages?
questions.answer: Packages typically use reversed domain names in lowercase (e.g., com.company.project) to ensure uniqueness.
questions.explanation: This avoids collisions across organizations and projects.

questions.question: Which of the following allows a class to expose only a 'contract' without implementation?
questions.answer: Interface
questions.explanation: Interfaces specify method signatures (contracts) while implementations are provided by classes.

questions.question: What is the role of the 'package-info.java' file?
questions.answer: package-info.java holds package-level annotations and documentation (package javadoc).
questions.explanation: It documents and annotates package metadata.

questions.question: When a subclass method calls 'super.method()', what happens?
options: Creates new object and calls its method
questions.answer: Invokes overridden superclass method
questions.explanation: super.method() calls the parent class's implementation of the method.

units.unit: Unit III - Exception Handling and Multithreading

questions.question: Which keyword is used to explicitly throw an exception?
questions.answer: throw
questions.explanation: throw is used to throw a new exception instance; throws is used in method signature to declare possible exceptions.

questions.question: Differentiate between checked and unchecked exceptions.
questions.answer: Checked exceptions must be declared or handled at compile time (e.g., IOException); unchecked exceptions are runtime errors (e.g., NullPointerException) not required to be declared.
questions.explanation: Checked exceptions extend Exception (not RuntimeException); unchecked extend RuntimeException or Error.

questions.question: What does the 'finally' block guarantee?
options: Executes whether or not exception occurred
questions.answer: Executes whether or not exception occurred
questions.explanation: finally runs after try/catch irrespective of exception, useful for cleanup.

questions.question: What is the significance of 'throws' clause in method declaration?
questions.answer: throws declares that a method may throw certain checked exceptions which callers must handle or re-declare.
questions.explanation: It informs the compiler and callers about potential checked exceptions.

questions.question: Which of these is a correct way to create a thread in Java?
options: Implement Runnable and pass to Thread
questions.answer: All of the above
questions.explanation: Multiple ways exist: subclass Thread, implement Runnable, or use higher-level concurrency utilities.

questions.question: What is thread synchronization and why is it used?
questions.answer: Synchronization controls access to shared resources to prevent thread interference and ensure data consistency.
questions.explanation: Synchronized blocks/methods serialize access to critical sections to avoid race conditions.

questions.question: Which method causes the current thread to pause execution for specified milliseconds?
questions.answer: sleep()
questions.explanation: Thread.sleep(ms) suspends current thread for given time; wait() is used with object monitors.

questions.question: Explain the life cycle states of a Thread briefly.
questions.answer: New (created), Runnable (ready or running), Blocked/Waiting (paused for monitor/condition), Timed Waiting (sleep/wait with timeout), Terminated (completed).
questions.explanation: Thread transitions via start(), wait/notify, sleep(), join(), and run completion.

questions.question: Which exception is thrown when you try to divide by zero using integer arithmetic?
questions.answer: ArithmeticException
questions.explanation: Integer division by zero raises ArithmeticException at runtime.

questions.question: What does 'throw new IllegalArgumentException("msg")' do?
questions.answer: It creates and throws an IllegalArgumentException with message 'msg' to indicate invalid method arguments.
questions.explanation: It signals caller about invalid parameters and stops normal flow unless caught.

questions.question: Which method is used to notify a single waiting thread from synchronized block?
questions.answer: notify()
questions.explanation: notify() wakes one waiting thread; notifyAll() wakes all waiting threads on the object's monitor.

questions.question: What is a custom (user-defined) exception and how is it created?
questions.answer: A custom exception is a class extending Exception or RuntimeException; create by extending and providing constructors, e.g., class MyException extends Exception {}
questions.explanation: Used to represent application-specific error conditions.

questions.question: Which keyword ensures a block of code is executed even if an exception occurs?
questions.answer: finally
questions.explanation: finally always executes after try/catch for cleanup activities.

questions.question: What is deadlock in multithreading?
questions.answer: Deadlock occurs when two or more threads are blocked forever waiting for resources held by each other, preventing progress.
questions.explanation: Occurs due to circular resource dependency and lack of proper ordering or timeouts.

questions.question: Which interface must be implemented to use a thread pool via Executors (basic)?
questions.answer: Runnable
questions.explanation: Runnable tasks can be submitted to ExecutorService; Callable is also used when tasks return values.

questions.question: What is the difference between Runnable and Callable?
questions.answer: Runnable's run() doesn't return a result or throw checked exceptions; Callable's call() returns a value and may throw checked exceptions.
questions.explanation: Use Callable for tasks needing results and exception handling.

questions.question: Which of these is true about synchronized methods?
options: They acquire object or class lock
They cannot call other synchronized methods
questions.answer: They acquire object or class lock
questions.explanation: Instance synchronized methods acquire object's monitor; static synchronized methods acquire class-level lock.

questions.question: How does 'volatile' keyword help in multithreading?
questions.answer: volatile ensures reads/writes to a variable go directly to main memory, guaranteeing visibility across threads but not atomicity.
questions.explanation: Use volatile for visibility of simple flags; for compound actions use synchronization/atomic types.

questions.question: Which exception must a method declare if it performs file I/O operations (checked exception example)?
questions.answer: IOException
questions.explanation: IO operations commonly throw checked IOException which must be handled or declared.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Thread.join()?
questions.answer: join() allows one thread to wait until another thread completes its execution.
questions.explanation: It synchronizes threads by pausing current thread until the joined thread terminates.

questions.question: Which class would you use for atomic integer operations without synchronization?
questions.answer: AtomicInteger
questions.explanation: java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger provides lock-free thread-safe operations.

questions.question: What is the effect of catching Throwable instead of Exception?
questions.answer: Catching Throwable catches all errors and exceptions, including serious Errors (like OutOfMemoryError), which is discouraged.
questions.explanation: Errors represent unrecoverable JVM conditions and should not be caught generally.

questions.question: Which method should be overridden when extending Thread class?
questions.answer: run()
questions.explanation: run() contains the code executed by the new thread; start() initiates the thread and calls run().

questions.question: Give a brief code snippet showing how to handle checked exception using try-catch.
questions.answer: Example: try { FileInputStream f = new FileInputStream("a.txt"); } catch (FileNotFoundException e) { e.printStackTrace(); }
questions.explanation: Wrap operations that throw checked exceptions in try and catch to handle errors gracefully.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a thread state?
questions.answer: Sleeping
questions.explanation: Sleeping is not an official Thread.State; Timed_Waiting or BLOCKED/WAITING are official states.

units.unit: Unit IV - Event handling using Abstract Window Toolkit (AWT) & Swing Components

questions.question: Which package contains Swing components?
questions.answer: javax.swing
questions.explanation: Swing components are in javax.swing package; AWT is in java.awt.

questions.question: What is the difference between AWT and Swing?
questions.answer: AWT is heavyweight and relies on native peers, while Swing is lightweight, written in Java, and offers more components and pluggable look-and-feel.
questions.explanation: Swing extends AWT event model but provides richer, platform-independent components.

questions.question: Which layout manager places components in five regions (North, South, East, West, Center)?
questions.answer: BorderLayout
questions.explanation: BorderLayout divides container into five regions supporting component placement.

questions.question: What is an ActionListener and how is it used?
questions.answer: ActionListener is an interface with actionPerformed(ActionEvent) method; add to buttons/menus to handle action events.
questions.explanation: Implement interface and register listener to components to receive action events like button clicks.

questions.question: Which Swing component is used to accept single line text input?
questions.answer: JTextField
questions.explanation: JTextField is for single-line text; JTextArea is for multi-line.

questions.question: What is delegation event model in Java GUI?
questions.answer: Delegation model separates event source and listener; listeners (delegates) register with sources to receive event objects.
questions.explanation: This model improves performance by notifying interested listeners only.

questions.question: Which listener would you use to detect key presses on a component?
questions.answer: KeyListener
questions.explanation: KeyListener receives keyPressed, keyReleased, keyTyped events for keyboard input.

questions.question: How do you show a message dialog in Swing?
questions.answer: Use JOptionPane.showMessageDialog(parentComponent, "Message"); to display simple message dialogs.
questions.explanation: JOptionPane provides ready-made dialogs for messages, input, and confirmations.

questions.question: Which container is typically the top-level window for a Swing application?
questions.answer: JFrame
questions.explanation: JFrame is a top-level window with decorations (title bar, close button) used for main application windows.

questions.question: What is the use of layout managers in GUI design?
questions.answer: Layout managers control component placement/resizing within containers across different screen sizes and platforms.
questions.explanation: They automate component layout instead of absolute positioning for responsiveness.

questions.question: Which component provides a drop-down list of choices in Swing?
questions.answer: JComboBox
questions.explanation: JComboBox displays a single selection from a drop-down list; JList shows multiple items.

questions.question: Explain the difference between repaint() and paintComponent().
questions.answer: repaint() requests a component redraw by scheduling a call; paintComponent(Graphics g) contains actual painting code invoked by the painting system.
questions.explanation: Override paintComponent for custom rendering; call repaint to request update.

questions.question: Which event is generated when a user selects a menu item?
questions.answer: ActionEvent
questions.explanation: Selecting menu items triggers ActionEvent handled by ActionListener.

questions.question: What is a JMenuBar and how is it used?
questions.answer: JMenuBar is a container for JMenu objects; set it on JFrame using setJMenuBar(menuBar) to add menus to the window.
questions.explanation: It organizes top-level menus like File, Edit, View in GUI applications.

questions.question: Which Swing component is used to display tabbed panes?
questions.answer: JTabbedPane
questions.explanation: JTabbedPane creates multiple tabs each containing different components or panels.

questions.question: Describe how to handle mouse click events on a component.
questions.answer: Implement MouseListener and override mouseClicked (or use MouseAdapter) then register with component using addMouseListener().
questions.explanation: MouseAdapter simplifies implementation by providing empty method bodies to override selectively.

questions.question: Which layout arranges components in a grid of equal-sized cells?
questions.answer: GridLayout
questions.explanation: GridLayout places components in rows and columns with equal cell sizes.

questions.question: What is an ItemListener used for?
questions.answer: ItemListener listens for item selection/deselection events on components like CheckBox or JComboBox (itemStateChanged).
questions.explanation: Useful for tracking changes in selection state of items.

questions.question: Which component would you use to present tabular data?
questions.answer: JTable
questions.explanation: JTable displays data in rows and columns and supports cell renderers/editors.

questions.question: How do you make a Swing GUI thread-safe at startup?
questions.answer: Create and show GUI on the Event Dispatch Thread using SwingUtilities.invokeLater(() -> createAndShowGUI());
questions.explanation: Swing components should be constructed and manipulated on EDT to avoid race conditions.

questions.question: Which of following is true about JFrame.setDefaultCloseOperation(JFrame.EXIT_ON_CLOSE)?
options: Exits the application when window closed
questions.answer: Exits the application when window closed
questions.explanation: EXIT_ON_CLOSE terminates the JVM when the frame is closed.

questions.question: What is a JScrollPane and when is it used?
questions.answer: JScrollPane provides scrollbars for components that may exceed visible area like large JTextArea or JTable.
questions.explanation: Wrap components in JScrollPane to allow scrolling when content is larger than view.

questions.question: Which event listener would you implement to handle changes in text components (simple)?
questions.answer: DocumentListener
questions.explanation: DocumentListener is more precise for text changes in Swing (tracks insert/remove/changed in Document).

questions.question: Explain how to create a simple calculator using GridLayout and buttons (brief steps).
questions.answer: Create JFrame, set GridLayout for button area, add JTextField for display, add numeric and operator JButton components, register ActionListeners to handle input and compute results.
questions.explanation: Use listeners to update display and perform calculations when operators or equals pressed.

questions.question: Which Swing component would you use for hierarchical display of nodes (like folders)?
questions.answer: JTree
questions.explanation: JTree displays hierarchical data such as file-system structures.

units.unit: Unit V - Basics of Network Programming

questions.question: Which class is used to get the IP address and host name of the local or remote host?
questions.answer: InetAddress
questions.explanation: InetAddress provides methods to get host name and IP address.

questions.question: Differentiate TCP and UDP in brief.
questions.answer: TCP is connection-oriented, reliable, and stream-based; UDP is connectionless, faster but unreliable and datagram-based.
questions.explanation: Use TCP for guaranteed delivery; UDP for low-latency or simple message exchange.

questions.question: Which class is used to create a server socket that listens for client connections (TCP)?
questions.answer: ServerSocket
questions.explanation: ServerSocket listens for incoming TCP connections; Socket represents client/server connection.

questions.question: What is a DatagramPacket used for?
questions.answer: DatagramPacket represents data packets sent/received via DatagramSocket for UDP communication.
questions.explanation: It encapsulates payload, destination address, and port for UDP datagrams.

questions.question: Which class is typically used to read content from a URL?
questions.answer: URL
questions.explanation: URL provides openStream() and connection methods to fetch resource content over network.

questions.question: How do you create a simple TCP client socket to connect to server at host 'host' and port 5000?
questions.answer: Socket client = new Socket("host", 5000);
questions.explanation: Instantiating Socket establishes TCP connection to specified host and port if reachable.

questions.question: Which method of InetAddress returns the local host address?
questions.answer: getLocalHost()
questions.explanation: InetAddress.getLocalHost() returns local host address and name.

questions.question: What is URLConnection used for?
questions.answer: URLConnection manages communication to a URL and can be used to read from or write to the resource represented by the URL.
questions.explanation: It provides methods to get input and output streams, content type, and metadata.

questions.question: Which socket type should be used for connectionless communication?
questions.answer: DatagramSocket
questions.explanation: DatagramSocket supports UDP connectionless datagram communication.

questions.question: Explain how to retrieve hostname and IP address using InetAddress.
questions.answer: Use InetAddress inet = InetAddress.getByName("host"); then inet.getHostName() and inet.getHostAddress().
questions.explanation: getByName resolves host and returns InetAddress for network queries.

questions.question: Which class would you use to create an HTTP connection and read response headers?
questions.answer: HttpURLConnection
questions.explanation: HttpURLConnection is subclass of URLConnection for HTTP-specific features (response codes, headers).

questions.question: What port range is called 'well-known' ports?
questions.answer: Ports 0–1023 are well-known ports reserved for common services.
questions.explanation: Reserved services like HTTP(80), FTP(21), SSH(22) use well-known ports.

questions.question: Which of the following is true for ServerSocket.accept()?
options: It blocks until a client connects and returns a Socket
questions.answer: It blocks until a client connects and returns a Socket
questions.explanation: accept() waits for incoming connection and returns a Socket for communication.

questions.question: What is the role of port number in networking?
questions.answer: Port number identifies a specific application/service on a host, allowing multiple services to run simultaneously on same IP.
questions.explanation: IP identifies host; port identifies service endpoint on that host.

questions.question: Which class supports multicast operations?
questions.answer: MulticastSocket
questions.explanation: MulticastSocket extends DatagramSocket with multicast group membership capabilities.

questions.question: Briefly describe how to send a UDP packet in Java.
questions.answer: Create DatagramSocket, create DatagramPacket with data and destination InetAddress/port, then socket.send(packet).
questions.explanation: DatagramPacket encapsulates payload and destination for UDP send/receive.

questions.question: Which method returns the content length from a URLConnection?
questions.answer: getContentLength()
questions.explanation: URLConnection.getContentLength() returns the content length in bytes (or -1 if not known).

questions.question: What is a proxy server and why might a client use one?
questions.answer: A proxy server intermediates client requests to the internet, used for caching, filtering, anonymity, or corporate network policies.
questions.explanation: Clients route requests via proxy to manage performance, control and security.

questions.question: Which class/feature should be used to download a web page content as a stream?
questions.answer: URL.openStream()
questions.explanation: URL.openStream() returns InputStream to read resource content from a URL.

questions.question: Explain how to extract components from URL using java.net.URL.
questions.answer: Use methods like getProtocol(), getHost(), getPort(), getPath(), getQuery() to obtain URL parts.
questions.explanation: URL class parses and provides access to structural components of a URL.

questions.question: Which class should be used to open a connection and set request method to GET?
questions.answer: HttpURLConnection
questions.explanation: Use HttpURLConnection and call setRequestMethod("GET") for HTTP GET requests.

questions.question: What is the significance of using Buffered streams over raw Input/Output streams in networking?
questions.answer: Buffered streams add buffering which reduces network calls and improves I/O performance by reading/writing larger blocks.
questions.explanation: Buffering minimizes system calls and network latency by grouping small reads/writes.

questions.question: Which exception commonly occurs when host cannot be resolved?
questions.answer: UnknownHostException
questions.explanation: UnknownHostException indicates DNS lookup failure or unknown host name.

questions.question: Write a brief client-server interaction sequence for TCP sockets.
questions.answer: Server creates ServerSocket and calls accept(); client creates Socket(host,port); server accept() returns Socket; both obtain streams and exchange data; then close sockets.
questions.explanation: This demonstrates connection establishment, data exchange, and termination.

questions.question: Which of the following is returned by URLConnection.getInputStream()?
questions.answer: InputStream
questions.explanation: getInputStream() returns InputStream to read resource bytes from server.

questions.question: Which class is used to register JDBC drivers and establish database connections?
questions.answer: DriverManager
questions.explanation: DriverManager.getConnection(url, user, pass) loads registered drivers and returns Connection.

questions.question: Name the four types of JDBC drivers briefly.
questions.answer: Type 1: JDBC-ODBC bridge, Type 2: native API, Type 3: network protocol, Type 4: pure Java (thin) driver.
questions.explanation: Type 4 drivers are platform independent and most commonly used in production.

questions.question: Which JDBC interface is used to execute an SQL query and return a ResultSet?
questions.answer: Statement
questions.explanation: Statement.executeQuery(sql) returns ResultSet; PreparedStatement can also execute queries with parameters.

questions.question: What are PreparedStatements and why are they preferred over Statements?
questions.answer: PreparedStatement precompiles SQL, allows parameter binding, improves performance, and prevents SQL injection.
questions.explanation: They are efficient for repeated queries and safer for user input.

questions.question: Which method of ResultSet moves the cursor to the next row?
questions.answer: next()
questions.explanation: ResultSet.next() advances cursor to next row and returns false when no more rows.

questions.question: Explain two-tier and three-tier JDBC architecture briefly.
questions.answer: Two-tier: client directly connects to DB via JDBC; Three-tier: client communicates with middle-tier server (application server) which interacts with DB, enabling scalability and separation of concerns.
questions.explanation: Three-tier adds middleware for business logic and reduced DB coupling from clients.

questions.question: Which interface provides metadata about the ResultSet columns?
questions.answer: ResultSetMetaData
questions.explanation: ResultSetMetaData gives info like column count, types, and labels.

questions.question: How do you load a JDBC driver (classic way)?
questions.answer: Class.forName("com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver"); which loads and registers the driver class (older approach).
questions.explanation: Recent JDBC versions auto-register drivers via Service Provider mechanism, but Class.forName still works.

questions.question: Which Connection method is used to disable auto-commit for transaction control?
questions.answer: setAutoCommit(false)
questions.explanation: Disabling auto-commit allows manual commit/rollback via commit() and rollback().

questions.question: Write the sequence of steps to perform an SQL SELECT query using JDBC.
questions.answer: Load driver, get Connection via DriverManager.getConnection, create Statement or PreparedStatement, executeQuery to get ResultSet, iterate ResultSet, close resources.
questions.explanation: Always close ResultSet, Statement, and Connection in finally block or use try-with-resources.

questions.question: Which exception type is commonly caught for JDBC operations?
questions.answer: SQLException
questions.explanation: JDBC operations throw SQLException for database access errors and other SQL related issues.

questions.question: What is ResultSet.TYPE_SCROLL_INSENSITIVE used for?
questions.answer: It creates a scrollable ResultSet that is not sensitive to underlying DB changes after creation.
questions.explanation: Allows navigation methods like previous(), absolute() without reflecting later DB updates.

questions.question: Which method is used to execute an update/insert/delete SQL command?
questions.answer: executeUpdate()
questions.explanation: executeUpdate returns number of affected rows for DML statements.

questions.question: How to use PreparedStatement to insert a record with parameters (brief)?
questions.answer: PreparedStatement ps = con.prepareStatement("INSERT INTO emp(id,name) VALUES(?,?)"); ps.setInt(1,id); ps.setString(2,name); ps.executeUpdate();
questions.explanation: Use parameter placeholders and setXXX methods to bind values safely.

questions.question: Which JDBC interface provides information about the database as a whole (product name, version)?
questions.answer: DatabaseMetaData
questions.explanation: DatabaseMetaData helps fetch DB capabilities and driver info.

questions.question: What is try-with-resources and how is it useful in JDBC?
questions.answer: Try-with-resources automatically closes AutoCloseable resources like Connection/Statement/ResultSet when block exits, preventing resource leaks.
questions.explanation: Simplifies cleanup and ensures proper closing even on exceptions.

questions.question: Which method of ResultSet is used to retrieve a column value as String?
questions.answer: getString()
questions.explanation: getString(columnIndexOrName) returns column value converted to String.

questions.question: What is connection pooling and why use it?
questions.answer: Connection pooling reuses a set of pre-created database connections to reduce overhead of establishing connections repeatedly, improving performance.
questions.explanation: Avoids expensive connection creation on each DB operation, especially for web apps.

questions.question: Which of following is correct to retrieve auto-generated keys after insert?
questions.answer: executeUpdate(sql, Statement.RETURN_GENERATED_KEYS) then getGeneratedKeys()
questions.explanation: Use RETURN_GENERATED_KEYS flag and call getGeneratedKeys() to fetch generated key(s).

questions.question: Why prefer PreparedStatement for repeated queries?
questions.answer: PreparedStatement is precompiled by DB, reducing parsing overhead for repeated executions and improving performance.
questions.explanation: Also helps prevent SQL injection and supports parameterization.

questions.question: Which JDBC URL format is commonly used for MySQL (connector/J)?
questions.answer: jdbc:mysql://host:port/dbname
questions.explanation: Standard JDBC URL format begins with jdbc:subprotocol://host:port/database.

questions.question: What is getConnection pooling advantage when using DataSource vs DriverManager?
questions.answer: DataSource can provide connection pooling and JNDI-managed connections, offering better performance and manageability than DriverManager.
questions.explanation: Application servers typically provide DataSource implementations with pooling.

questions.question: Which method in Connection is used to permanently save transaction changes to database?
questions.answer: commit()
questions.explanation: commit finalizes transaction when auto-commit is disabled.

questions.question: Explain how to retrieve multiple rows from ResultSet (brief code idea).
questions.answer: ResultSet rs = stmt.executeQuery(sql); while (rs.next()) { int id = rs.getInt("id"); String name = rs.getString("name"); // process }
questions.explanation: Iterate rs.next() to move cursor row by row and fetch column values.

questions.question: Which method of Statement executes SQL that may return multiple result sets or update counts?
questions.answer: execute()
questions.explanation: execute() handles general SQL and you can inspect results via getResultSet() or getUpdateCount().
